full_judgment:
Md Khasruzzaman J: This first appeal has been preferred by the plaintiff against the judgment and decree dated 4-7-2013 (decree signed on 8-7-20l3) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.838 of 2012 rejecting the plaint under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 33. The facts of the case reported in 7 BLC (AD) 101 that the plaintiff had given a power of attorney to his uncle defendant No. 1 for running his business in the shop premises situated at Mohammadpur Kacha Bazar due to preoccupation elsewhere. The shop was allotted to the plaintiff by the defendant No.3, Deputy Commissioner, Housing and Settlement Directorate, for running grocery shop. "The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration that the sale deed dated 26-10-1981 executed by the petitioner No.1 on the basis of power of attorney of the plaintiff described in the Schedule A to the plaint is void, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff and' recovery of the khas possession of the shop No. 98 at Mohammdpur Kacha Bazar allotted by the defendant No.3 for running grocery shop. The plaintiff entrusted his uncle to look after and manage his business in the aforesaid shop and registered a power of attorney on 14-3-1981 for the said business. The plaintiff came to know that defendant No.1 has created fraudulent sale deed in favour of his wife defendant No.2 in respect of the suit shop by execution and registration of sale deed dated 26-10-1981. The plaintiff after getting the said information revoked the said power of attorney dated 14-3-1981 by a registered revocation deed dated 5-1-1984. It transpires that the defendant No.1 got a clause inserted in the power of attorney to the effect that he. could transfer of the shop room, the said clause is in violation of the terms and condition of the allotment and the plaintiff did not confer such power on the defendant No.1 Defendant No.3 has not yet been executed any title deed in favour of the plaintiff. The fraudulent insertion of clause as to transfer has been done subsequently and in violation of the terms and conditions of the allotment. There was no consideration for the said transfer in favour of the defendant No.2. The deed of sale executed by the defendant No.1 in favour of his wife defendant No.2 is also collusive and illegal and without any consideration and not binding upon the plaintiff.
